status: Two explicit interop levels: KarpathyShortRun executes pinned original definitions and the functional C# trainer; KarpathyByteParity independently verifies exact NumPy state. Centralized run outcomes remain separate.
license_observation: Original header declares BSD License; this is not a separately verified full license text.

reference_probe.source_scope: Full source read; independently expressed mathematical references executed, not Python2 top-level file IO/infinite loop.

assertions: Sorted vocabulary encoding/decoding, exact counts and rejected unknown tokens.
limits: Unspecified input.txt is replaced with an explicit tiny corpus; sorted UTF-16 character order replaces Python's nondeterministic set order.

assertions: Original hidden size100 and sequence length25, with stated five-character input fixture.
All 25 hidden states, probability distributions, accumulated loss, final state and five gradient arrays checked against live NumPy.
limits: The source does not supply a concrete corpus, initialization seed or recorded loss; no historical output is invented.

assertions: Pre-port NumPy2.4.2 reference loss5.54474603545919 for H3/V4/seed7 and four tokens.
Full forward arrays, probability normalization, initial-state preservation, exact live comparison on strided initial state.
All40 small-model trainable scalars checked by independent central finite differences (epsilon1e-5, absolute error1e-8).
Each of Wxh/Whh/Why/bh/by gradients compared with live NumPy on small and source-sized problems.
Explicit gradient entries beyond both bounds become exactly -5 and5; all five arrays checked.
Clipped derivative arrays match NumPy byte-for-byte.
Every accumulator update is g*g and every parameter follows learning-rate0.1 / sqrt(memory+1e-8).
Two consecutive updates compared for all five parameter arrays and all five persistent memories.
All original200 sample draws at hidden100 compared as exact token indices against live NumPy.
Twenty-token seeded small-model sequence recorded independently and asserted; initial state preserved.
limits: Samples are from explicit seeded numerical models, not an unidentified historical corpus or checkpoint.

assertions: 40 complete updates of a real H16 RNN on 'hello world\n' repeated40times, sequence25, learning-rate0.1, initialization seed1.
All40 losses, smoothed losses, positions and reset flags compared; all trained parameters/memories and final hidden state compared.
Loss decreases from54.929665653107975 to0.6994428739514988 in the independently measured reference; no monotonic-improvement promise.
Resets at0/19/38 and40-token pre-update samples at0/20 are asserted.
limits: The original infinite loop is replaced with a required finite iteration count; the demo uses H16 and shorter periodic samples, while separate tests cover original H100/sequence25/sample200 settings.
No external input.txt is read and no original unbounded run is executed.

assertions: Model parameters, optimizer memories, gradients and returned states survive disposal of an enclosing temporary NDScope.
Each owning model/result implements IDisposable; borrowed properties do not transfer ownership.
Actual Demo prints480characters, vocabulary9, hidden16 and40updates.
Both printed losses are parsed and checked against independently observed NumPy results.
All characters in the two actual printed samples are asserted, not merely their lengths.
Hash-pinned original lossFun and sample execute inside the pythonnet interpreter, not replacement Python equations.
Four complete H100/sequence25 updates over an explicit65-token corpus include hidden-state carry/reset, clipped BPTT, all five Adagrad memories, smoothed losses and48 sampled tokens.
The actual C# Train API also executes the same short workload; all four functional losses equal the original run, all samples are valid, reset boundaries and state changes are asserted.
The first original NumPy2.4.2 loss was independently probed as17.318640025562782 before adding the test.
limits: The loader checks original SHA256 and selects only lossFun/sample definitions after Python2 syntax adaptation; source imports, input.txt IO and while True are never executed.
Sampling every step with12tokens is an explicit bounded branch-coverage fixture; the existing test separately covers the original200-draw sample size.
This aggressive four-update fixture exercises real clipping and is not a claim of monotonic loss improvement or a historical-corpus reproduction.

assertions: At every one of four updates, dtype/shape/canonical bytes are checked for loss, smoothed loss, data position and reset flag; all48 samples; every forward hidden/probability value; and carried hidden state.
All five raw gradient arrays and all five clipped arrays are compared before every optimizer update; the fixture must actually exceed the clipping bound.
All five parameter arrays and all five Adagrad memories are checked after every update, replacing the earlier final-state-only gap.
Both engines start from the same zero-copy-exported parameter bits, then evolve independent owned buffers; no updated C# state is used to create its own oracle.
limits: The independent NumPy reference is separate from the original-source functional level. No tolerance fallback exists.

The original five interop executions remain as explicit KarpathyByteParity tests, including the40-update loss trace, original100x25 forward/BPTT dimensions,200-draw sampling and two-update Adagrad gate.

exclusions.reason: No original input.txt, vocabulary enumeration seed or output transcript is available. The port is a full functioning RNN, but its explicit corpus and generated samples are not represented as historical author outputs.
Unbounded training is replaced by a finite caller-selected number of iterations. All update/reset/smoothing/sampling behavior within the chosen finite run is functional.
